integration_test.original_failure_reason: The first combined command named a nonexistent scripts.tests.test_application_qmp_capture module; no production/source failure occurred and the corrected command used scripts.tests.test_qmp_capture.

verified_behavior: After Popen and before ownership transfer, the backend captures positive QEMU PID, PGID, session ID and robustly parsed /proc starttime; PID, PGID and session must match the new-session leader
Capture or transfer failure follows existing TERM, WNOWAIT observation, KILL and exact reap recovery while preserving the original error
The lifecycle retains primitive QEMU identity after exact reap and the evaluator rejects missing, malformed or mismatched identity
The outer owner queues its positive process identity, acquired root-lock device/inode/mode/link/owner identity and exact validated cgroup values in memory
Outer evidence publication remains deferred until authenticated container absence and lock release
The owner source binds the new diagnostic and backend hashes
limitations: Tests establish parser/schema and Python-child ownership behavior, not actual QEMU identity capture
QEMU identity reaches the final result only on successful evaluation; failure paths retain their existing raw process/capture evidence
Outer starttime explicitly permits null if procfs is unavailable; the actual packet must require a non-null value on this host
Uncertain create or client retirement intentionally prevents evidence flush and retains the live owner/lock identity
This is source readiness only, not execution release or OS/application acceptance
next_action: Shorten the attempt root so qmp.sock is at most 107 bytes, update all packet source hashes and evidence limits, then obtain a fresh independent one-shot execution review.
